chunks: And from him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakam, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to the woman from behind (in the rear), he said, 'There is no harm with it.'

key_terms.دُبُرِهَا: her rear (referring to the dorsal position in intercourse)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm with it / it is permissible
key_terms.يَأْتِي: he comes to / has intercourse with

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to have intercourse with his wife from behind according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the permissibility of the dorsal position in marital relations, reflecting the Shia view that sexual acts are permissible unless explicitly prohibited by text or reason. The concise ruling ('la ba'sa bihi') underscores the flexibility and lack of ritual restriction in this specific act, distinguishing it from acts that might require specific purification or carry disapproval. This ruling is often cited in fiqh discussions regarding the general permissibility of intercourse in all parts of the body except the anus.
